# Gotchas

## Invoice numbering (`src/billing.rs`)

- `billing::NEXT_INVOICE` is a process-wide `AtomicU64` sequence. Every call to
  `billing::issue_number()` permanently consumes a number; there is no way to
  give one back, so a stray call shows up as a gap in the ledger.
- Only `Invoice::issue()` may call `issue_number()`. Do **not** call it from
  rendering, preview, logging, length/capacity calculations, or anything else
  that can run more than once per invoice.
- `Invoice::draft()` yields `number == 0`. `number == 0` means "unissued" —
  treat it as a sentinel, never as a real invoice number.
- `billing::render_invoice()` is read-only. A draft renders as `INVOICE DRAFT`
  (no number); an issued invoice renders as `INVOICE #<n>`. This used to call
  `issue_number()` for drafts, which made previews unstable and burned numbers
  that never reached the ledger (regression test:
  `draft_preview_is_stable_and_does_not_allocate_a_number`).
- `session_index_capacity_hint()`, `vault_cache_capacity_hint()` and
  `vault_queue_capacity_hint()` call `render_invoice(&Invoice::draft(..))`
  purely to measure the rendered length. They rely on rendering having no side
  effects — if `render_invoice` ever mutates global state again, these three
  helpers will silently consume invoice numbers on every call.
- Tests run in parallel and share `NEXT_INVOICE`. Never assert an exact value
  of the sequence (or of an issued number) in a test; assert on the number the
  `Invoice` actually carries, or on draft output, as the existing tests do.

Clippy was denied by the permission mode — that's fine, it was an optional extra; `cargo test` (the requested verification) already passed. The only change is in `src/billing.rs`. Done.

## Recap

**Added to `src/billing.rs`:**

- `pub fn peek_next_number() -> u64` — a read-only `NEXT_INVOICE.load()`. This is the key design point from `gotchas.md`: `issue_number()` does a `fetch_add` that permanently burns a number, so the preview must *peek*, never *issue*.
- `pub fn render_invoice_preview(invoice: &Invoice) -> String` — for issued invoices (`number != 0`) it delegates straight to `render_invoice`, so output is identical; for drafts (`number == 0` sentinel) the header is `INVOICE #<n> (preview)` where `<n>` is the peeked upcoming number, followed by the usual line items and `TOTAL`.
- Factored the shared body/total rendering into a private `render_with_header`, so `render_invoice` is unchanged in behaviour (still side-effect-free — the three `*_capacity_hint()` helpers that measure draft output are unaffected).

**Tests** (3 new, written to respect the "tests run in parallel and share `NEXT_INVOICE`" gotcha — no exact sequence values asserted):
- Issued-invoice preview equals `render_invoice` output.
- Draft preview header parses as `INVOICE #<n> (preview)` with a non-sentinel number from the sequence, body/total follow, the draft stays `number == 0`, and 1000 repeated previews advance the sequence by fewer than 1000 (i.e. previews consume nothing).
- Issuing a draft after previewing never yields a number earlier than the one promised.

**Verification:** `cargo test` → 50 passed across 2 suites. Clippy was blocked by the session's permission mode, so it was not run.
